claim: Overfitting definition
quote: Overfitting is when a model describes noise rather than signal. The model may have good performance on the data on which it was tested, but little or no predictive power on new data in the future.

claim: Controls named: range of models, complexity penalty, parameter stability, independent review, rejection rate
quote: Common methods to deal with overfitting include: using a range of models instead of relying on a single one (model confidence set), penalizing models for complexity, considering model stability under parameter variation, an independent review process, and monitoring the rejection rate of strategies through the review process

claim: Parameter heat-map test
quote: you modify the model parameters and look at the corresponding ‘heat maps', and assess how performance changes when varying the parameters. If your parameter choice is an isolated point sticking out, then this is a red flag and suggests the parameter choice was a result of data mining.

claim: Rejection-rate monitoring across research, review, test trading
quote: There's the concept of the rejection rate, so basically monitoring how many strategies are proposed originally, and how far they make it through the process. How many don't survive the initial research phase, how many are killed during review, and how many don't make it past test trading - monitoring this rate can be an important asset.

claim: Written-in-advance data partitioning, methodology and expectations at AHL

claim: Strategies first traded with firm capital

claim: Test trading 2-3 months, not a significance test; catches mistakes; drawdown inconsistency
quote: the 2-3 months we would typically test trade a new model is not enough time to demonstrate any kind of statistical significance around the performance. However there have been a number of occasions where this process has caught ‘bad' strategies. This could uncover a mistake in the research or the implementation. A model immediately going into a large drawdown would certainly be a warning sign. For models with high expected Sharpe ratios we can be more certain: for example a 20% drawdown over the first three months would certainly look inconsistent with an assumed SR of 3.

claim: Common break across strategies = regime shift; single break = overfit
quote: If you have a range of strategies, and you see the same breaking point across all of them simultaneously, then a regime shift is likely. If, however, the breaking point only appears for one strategy then it is more likely due to overfitting.

claim: Expected live Sharpe band from model error
quote: If I'm trading with a Sharpe of one, and I think my overfitting/ model error consensus Sharpe is ±0.2, then as a professional I would be surprised if I didn't achieve 0.8 in trading, but I would also be surprised if I surpassed a Sharpe ratio of 1.2.

claim: Reward high-quality negative results; data-access tracking safeguards can be bypassed

claim: CERN practices: artificial datasets, control regions, strict IS/OOS, replication

claim: Worked example: SR 1.0, 120 months, 100 tests, rho 0.4 -> BHY SR 0.438, haircut 52.0%
